decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already captures the necessary high-speed mixing constraint that mixing remain smooth rather than overly aggressive.

The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the 5200 RPM maximum, prohibition on continuous maximum-speed operation, and adjustable slow-mixing and higher-speed-frothing modes; the splash-control change adds no further speed-control state.
The client only identifies bowl-depth adjustment as a conditional mitigation option and does not change the current bowl depth, capacity, or geometry.
A possible whisk-position adjustment does not change the selected whisk head's material, style, size, or fine-powder design requirements.
The source concerns splashing and mixing behavior at higher motor speeds, not dispensing flow, sputtering, dripping, beverage preservation, or the pour sequence.
The higher-speed splash-control decision does not affect the placard text, position, or customer-facing orientation.
The source does not change whether the spout is removable or its cleaning purpose.
Approval of higher-speed operation and conditional mechanical splash mitigation does not change the required wiring plan or its documented level of detail.
The source does not alter the solenoid-valve actuation mechanism or button-controlled dispensing behavior.
Conditional adjustment of bowl depth for splash mitigation does not necessarily alter easy bowl removal or rapid bowl swapping.
The candidate records the BOM and component-selection deliverables rather than individual selected motor specifications, so the source decision leaves its current requirement state unchanged.
Controlling splashing at higher speeds does not modify the independent requirement that the bottom bowl seal prevent liquid from reaching the electronics.
